CityHub.body:
Panama City eats like a capital that never settled on a single identity, and that is exactly the appeal. In the old town of Casco Viejo, colonial courtyards hide tasting menus, rooftop bars and Panamanian fondas within a few cobbled blocks. Cross into Bella Vista and El Cangrejo and the mood turns dense and late, with cevicherias, izakayas, cantinas and some of the city's best value sitting shoulder to shoulder. Costa del Este brings the glossy, modern side, its international kitchens built for the business crowd, while Amador looks back at the skyline over seafood and a bay breeze.

Seafood and ceviche are the through-line almost everywhere, shaped by two oceans and a canal that pulls cooks in from around the world. Italian, Peruvian, Japanese, Lebanese and Venezuelan tables sit comfortably beside sancocho and ropa vieja. Prices run the full range, from a few dollars for patacones at a counter to a proper splurge in Casco. Use the map to see how the neighborhoods sit, then open any one to browse every restaurant we track there and filter by cuisine, price or occasion.

CityHub.sceneTitle: Five scenes, a short drive apart
CityHub.scene: Panama City doesn't have one food scene - it has five, and they're a short drive apart. In Casco Viejo, the old town, colonial courtyards hide tasting menus and rooftop bars; it's where you go when the meal is the night. Cross into El Cangrejo and Bella Vista and the mood flips - dense, late and cheap in the best way, with cevicherias and izakayas shoulder to shoulder. Costa del Este is the glossy, modern side, built for the business crowd and international kitchens. Amador trades the city for a bay breeze and seafood over the skyline. Underneath all of it runs the same thread: ceviche and the day's catch, shaped by two oceans and a canal that has pulled cooks here from everywhere. Prices run the whole ladder, from a two-dollar plate of patacones to a proper splurge in Casco - so the real question isn't how much, it's which night you're having.
CityHub.eatTitle: The dishes that define Panama City
CityHub.eatSub: Come hungry for these - the plates you'll see on tables all over town.
CityHub.dish1Desc: Corvina cured in lime, onion and cilantro. The national way to start a meal.
CityHub.dish2Desc: Sea bass, grilled or fried whole - the default fish on almost every menu.
CityHub.dish3Desc: Chicken-and-culantro soup with yam. The Sunday cure, eaten year round.
CityHub.dish4Desc: Slow-shredded beef in tomato and pepper, served over white rice.
CityHub.dish5Desc: Twice-fried green plantains, salted. They come with almost everything.
CityHub.dish6Desc: The everyday chicken-and-rice plate - Panama's comfort default.
CityHub.knowSub: The practical stuff locals take for granted.
CityHub.prac1Desc: From a $2 plate of patacones at a fonda to $80+ tasting menus in Casco Viejo. Most of the city sits in a comfortable middle.
CityHub.prac2Desc: Walk in most places. Book ahead for Casco Viejo dining rooms and weekend rooftops - many spots take reservations over WhatsApp.
CityHub.prac3Desc: Dinner runs late, with kitchens busiest from 8 to 10pm. Lunch, noon to 2, is the value window for menu del dia deals.
CityHub.prac4Desc: Many bills already include a 10% service charge (propina). Check before you add more; rounding up for good service is normal.

faqA1Bullets: Special dinner or rooftops - Casco Viejo
Late, cheap and lively - El Cangrejo and Bella Vista
Modern and international - Costa del Este
CityHub.faqA1End: Pick the area that fits your plan, then open it to see every spot.
faqA2Bullets: El Cangrejo and Bella Vista - the densest nightlife (the Zona Viva)
faqA3Bullets: Casco Viejo - cevicherias and proper seafood dining
Amador - the day's catch with a bay view
CityHub.faqA3End: Order corvina (sea bass) or a lime-cured ceviche to start, or filter any area by Seafood.
faqA4Bullets: A few dollars - patacones at a counter or a menu del dia lunch
$15 to $30 - a solid sit-down dinner in most areas
$60 and up - a tasting menu in Casco Viejo
CityHub.faqA4End: Use the price filter on any neighborhood page. Many bills add a 10% service charge.

CityHub.faqQ6: What is Panama City known for, food-wise?
CityHub.faqA6: Two oceans and a canal shaped it, so:
faqA6Bullets: Seafood and ceviche, especially corvina (sea bass)
Panamanian comfort food - sancocho, ropa vieja, arroz con pollo, patacones
A deep international mix - Italian, Peruvian, Japanese, Lebanese and Venezuelan tables
CityHub.faqA6End: Start with a ceviche, then follow whichever kitchen the neighborhood is known for.
